1.e4 c5 2.f4 Nc6 3.Nf3.strategy: Develops the knight to its natural square and covers e5 and d4, the squares Black's knight and c-pawn would like to use. Nothing is committed yet: White can still choose between a positional squeeze and a kingside attack.

1.e4 c5 2.f4 Nc6 3.Nf3 g6.strategy: The modern main line: Black fianchettoes the king's bishop to control the long diagonal and hit the centre from a distance instead of occupying it. It also keeps the king compact and the position sound against White's attacking set-up.

1.e4 c5 2.f4 Nc6 3.Nf3 e6.name: Sicilian Defence: McDonnell Attack
1.e4 c5 2.f4 Nc6 3.Nf3 e6.strategy: Prepares to challenge e4 with the d-pawn and opens the f8 bishop. A solid, flexible set-up: Black keeps the pawn structure compact and waits to see how White uses the f-pawn advance.

1.e4 c5 2.f4 Nc6 3.Nf3 e6 4.d3.name: Sicilian Defence: McDonnell Attack
1.e4 c5 2.f4 Nc6 3.Nf3 e6 4.d3.strategy: Backs the e4 pawn and frees the c1 bishop. White chooses a restrained set-up, keeping the pawn centre compact and building towards a kingside attack rather than rushing it.

1.e4 c5 2.f4 Nc6 3.Nf3 g6 4.Bb5.strategy: Attacks the knight that holds d4 and e5 and threatens to take it and double Black's pawns. A positional approach: White fights for the central squares first and has no need to hurry the kingside attack.

1.e4 c5 2.f4 Nc6 3.Nf3 g6 4.Bb5 Bg7.name: Sicilian Defence: McDonnell Attack
1.e4 c5 2.f4 Nc6 3.Nf3 g6 4.Bb5 Bg7.strategy: Completes the fianchetto and ignores the pressure on c6: the knight is guarded twice by pawns, and a trade would only give Black the bishop pair for doubled pawns. Meanwhile the bishop controls the long diagonal, including d4 and e5.

1.e4 c5 2.f4 Nc6 3.Nf3 g6 4.Bb5 Bg7 5.c3.strategy: Takes d4 away from the black knight, so ...Nd4 can no longer chase the bishop, and prepares a broad pawn centre. White keeps the bishop and the option of a big centre rather than trading it off, at the cost of a slower attack.

1.e4 c5 2.f4 Nc6 3.Nf3 g6 4.Bb5 Bg7 5.Bx.strategy: Trades the bishop for the knight to double Black's pawns, but gives Black the bishop pair and, after the recapture, a half-open b-file. The doubled pawns are a lasting flaw, though not a decisive one, and White gives up the piece that was applying the pressure.

Recaptures with the b-pawn, which keeps the d-pawn free to move and opens the b-file for a rook. The doubled c-pawns are a structural flaw, but Black has the bishop pair and a solid grip on the centre.

1.e4 c5 2.f4 Nc6 3.Nf3 g6 4.Bb5 Bg7 5.c3.name: Sicilian Defence: McDonnell Attack
1.e4 c5 2.f4 Nc6 3.Nf3 g6 4.Bb5 Bg7 5.c3.strategy: Develops and attacks the e4 pawn, which nothing defends. White must deal with it before the central plan can go ahead, while Black completes development with tempo.

1.e4 c5 2.f4 Nc6 3.Nf3 g6 4.Bb5 Bg7 5.Bx.strategy: Brings the king to safety and the rook behind the advanced f-pawn, in line with White's kingside attacking plan, instead of spending time on the damaged black structure.
Backs the c5 pawn, covers e5 against White's f4 pawn and knight, and frees the bishop on c8. Black builds a compact, flexible pawn formation to put the doubled pawns to work in the centre.
